additions.what: Added explicit mention of covariate shift between treatment/control groups as a critical overlooked issue
additions.why: Student completely missed that the paper uses weighted conformal inference to handle covariate shift - this addition points to the problem without revealing the solution

additions.what: Added 'without requiring Bayesian priors' to first desirable property
additions.why: Student proposed a Bayesian approach when the paper is entirely frequentist - this gently steers away from Bayesian methods

additions.what: Added property about handling covariate shift between treatment/control groups
additions.why: This is central to the paper's weighted conformal approach but was not explicit in the original hint

additions.what: Added property about exact coverage for randomized experiments with known treatment assignment
additions.why: This is a key result of the paper that the student missed - it hints at leveraging known propensity scores

additions.what: Added property about validity when either outcome OR treatment model is misspecified
additions.why: This hints at the doubly robust property without naming it explicitly

additions.what: Added mention of 'distribution-free prediction methods' in field context
additions.why: Points toward conformal inference as the relevant methodology without naming it

removals.what: Removed 'account for both inherent variability and uncertainty due to finite sample estimation' as a separate property
removals.why: This is already captured in other properties and the student understood this aspect well

rationale.unchanged: Kept the core problem framing about moving beyond average effects, the fundamental problem of missing counterfactuals, and the inadequacy of existing uncertainty quantification methods, as these aspects were well understood by the student
